title: Trump Signals 'Decision Time' on Iran as Middle East Tensions Reach Boiling Point
snippet: President Donald Trump says he is weighing a diplomatic agreement against potential military action to 'finish off' Iranian threats, as the U.S. bolsters its naval presence in the Persian Gulf.
content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump warned that "decision time" is fast approaching regarding the U.S. stance on Iran, weighing a potential diplomatic agreement against renewed military action to eliminate escalating threats in the Middle East.

Speaking in an interview on Fox News' Sunday Morning Futures, Trump laid out a stark choice for Washington as Iranian-backed forces and Houthi militants in Yemen intensify targeted attacks against American and allied interests.

"I have a decision to make: Do I finish it off, which would be very easy to do, or do I make a deal? That's all," Trump declared. "We don't play games."

Surging Military Assets and Strategic Drawdowns

In anticipation of further escalation, the U.S. military has bolstered its deterrence posture in the region, sending a third aircraft carrier strike group toward the Persian Gulf. At the same time, federal agencies are quietly reducing non-essential diplomatic and military personnel in high-vulnerability areas across the Middle East.

State Department and defense officials confirmed that staffing shifts are underway in response to aggressive maneuvers by Iranian forces and proxies, particularly near the strategic Strait of Hormuz, where international commercial shipping has faced renewed disruptions.

A High-Stakes Timeline

National security experts and administration officials warn that the period following the November midterm elections could prove exceptionally volatile. Analysts view the stretch between Election Day and the inauguration of the new Congress as a critical window during which Tehran could test American resolve—or when Washington might launch decisive strikes if diplomatic talks fail to materialize.
